pipeline_stage_counts.name: Rooms by status
pipeline_stage_counts.limitation: A status is where a room is, not how far it has travelled. A room that has sat in Watching for a year looks identical here to one opened this morning.

funnel_progression.name: Stages reached
funnel_progression.limitation: Rooms can be reopened, so this is not a one-way funnel: a room counts once for each stage it ever reached, not once per visit. A recent window is incomplete by construction — rooms opened last week have not had time to reach a signing.

trial_process.name: Trial process
trial_process.limitation: These are counts of process steps in the window — invitations sent, accepted, schedules confirmed, trials completed, cancelled or declined — never how a trial went. No rate is built on them: a club that invites five players and completes three has not "converted 60%", it has run three trials.

decision_outcomes.name: Formal decisions
decision_outcomes.limitation: Counts of formal recruitment decisions finalized in the window, by outcome — progress, hold, reject — and how many were later superseded. A process count, never a verdict on anyone: a club that rejects nine players and progresses one has run ten decisions, not ranked ten people.

journey_evidence_funnel.name: Journey stages (from the records)
journey_evidence_funnel.limitation: Each stage counts cases for which the record itself exists — a delivered contact, a completed trial, a submitted assessment, a finalized decision, an issued or answered Offer, a completed signing — not cases whose status merely says so. A case counts once per stage however many retries or revisions it carried. Cases whose history reached a stage with no record behind it are shown apart as "history only"; they are older cases, not progress. A recent window is incomplete by construction.

exit_reason_mix.name: Why rooms ended
exit_reason_mix.limitation: This is the reason the club recorded, not the reason that operated. A decision carrying codes in two categories counts in both, so the shares add up to more than 100%.

time_to_first_decision.name: Time to first decision
time_to_first_decision.limitation: Rooms that never reached a decision are excluded, so this measures the rooms that got there. The number excluded is shown beside it.

time_in_stage.name: Time spent in each stage
time_in_stage.limitation: Only completed visits count. A stage where everything is stuck therefore looks fast, because only the rooms that escaped it are measured — Stalled rooms is the figure that catches that.

time_to_trial_requested.name: Time from opening to trial requested
time_to_trial_requested.limitation: A club that opens rooms late in its own process looks fast here. This measures the ScoutBox record, not the club’s thinking.

time_trial_requested_to_completed.name: Trial requested to completed
time_trial_requested_to_completed.limitation: Guardian response, pitch availability and school holidays all live inside this number and cannot be separated from it.

open_room_age.name: Age of open rooms
open_room_age.limitation: Age is not neglect. A long-running room on a fourteen-year-old being tracked to sixteen is the product working as intended.

stalled_rooms.name: Rooms with no recent activity
stalled_rooms.limitation: No activity in ScoutBox is not no activity. A scout who watched a player on Saturday and did not write it down produces a stalled room. This is a prompt to look, not a finding.

overdue_trial_reports.name: Trial reports past due
overdue_trial_reports.limitation: This surfaces an obligation the server already enforces — unfiled reports block new trial requests. It adds no new judgement.

decision_outstanding.name: Offers with no recorded decision
decision_outstanding.limitation: This reuses the Recruitment Room’s own readiness rule. If that rule is wrong, this is wrong in exactly the same way — deliberately, so there is one definition rather than two.

terminal_with_recorded_decision.name: Endings with a recorded decision
terminal_with_recorded_decision.limitation: Ending a room for a reason-required status records a decision automatically, so this rate is high by construction. Its value is in the exceptions.

superseded_decision_rate.name: Decisions later revised
superseded_decision_rate.limitation: Revising a decision is healthy. A high figure here is not a fault and is never coloured as one.

evidence_limited_exits.name: Endings limited by evidence
evidence_limited_exits.limitation: Association only. It does not follow that collecting the missing evidence would have changed any of these decisions.

reopen_rate.name: Rooms reopened after ending
reopen_rate.limitation: Reopening is intended behaviour — Second Look exists to cause it. High is not bad.

briefs_live.name: Live recruitment briefs
briefs_live.limitation: A brief being live says nothing about whether anyone is working it.

nobody_missed_backlog.name: Unreviewed eligible players
nobody_missed_backlog.limitation: The backlog is a function of how wide the brief is. Widening a brief creates backlog without anyone having done anything wrong.

nobody_missed_review_rate.name: Eligible players reviewed
nobody_missed_review_rate.limitation: Dismissing a candidate counts as reviewing them. This measures that the club looked, not what it concluded.

second_look_backlog.name: Open Second Look items
second_look_backlog.limitation: An expired item is not backlog — expiry is a designed outcome and is counted separately.

second_look_response_time.name: Time to respond to Second Look
second_look_response_time.limitation: Items never touched are absent from this figure. Their count is shown beside it.

room_source_mix.name: Where rooms came from
room_source_mix.limitation: Direct is the fallback ScoutBox assigns to anything it does not recognise, so it is a residual bucket rather than a surface people used.

source_stage_reach.name: Stages reached, by source
source_stage_reach.limitation: Confounded by construction, and never a ranking of surfaces: sources are listed alphabetically. Most will be withheld for too few rooms, which is the correct outcome rather than a gap.

active_watchlists.name: Active dynamic watchlists
active_watchlists.limitation: A big list is a wide set of criteria, nothing more.

watchlist_membership_churn.name: Players entering and leaving lists
watchlist_membership_churn.limitation: ScoutBox does not recompute watchlists in the background: membership is worked out when someone opens a list. This counts those recalculations, not the moment a player’s facts changed — a list nobody opens records no change at all.

ASSOCIATION_NOTE: ScoutBox observes that these records share this property and later reached this stage. It does not show that the property caused it: people choose where to look, and the players they find differ in ways ScoutBox does not measure.
